description: Square four-post canopy module roofed in overlapping nipa palm thatch, low gabled, open on all sides -- one bay of a covered market row.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Square four-post canopy module with a low gabled roof of overlapping nipa palm thatch panels, slender round timber posts at the four corners carrying a simple beam frame, open on all sides Materials: Sun-bleached grey-brown nipa palm leaf thatch laid in overlapping courses, fronds fraying and splitting at the eaves, darker damp underside, weathered hardwood posts with rope lashings at the joints.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.87. 1,592/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. Open on all four sides: turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement and a holeviz read per azimuth showing the red over the gable voids and brace bays only.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope measured 4.000 x 3.200 x 4.000 m off the built module, nothing crossing the cell edge on either axis; four 150 mm posts at +-1.913 with their outer faces on 2.000 less the lashing; head frame 2.06-2.22, eave 2.40, thatch apex 3.13, ridge plank top 3.200; low gable with the ridge along X; open on all four sides.
featureReviews.notes: Two deliberate divergences from the proxy, both recorded in envelopeDerivation: no eave overhang (a 4 m grid bay that overhangs collides with its neighbour) and an eave at 0.75 H rather than the proxy's 0.61, which caps the pitch at 20.0 degrees against 39.

featureReviews.evidence: One 20 x 12 height grid carrying both slopes; five courses per 1.60 m tile with a per-column jittered butt, a lit-tip line over a shadow gradient, six thinned gaps; ragged eave as a 0-110 mm per-column drop in the last rows -- real silhouette, no modelled fronds. Rendered 145-148 on the up-facing slope against the plate's own sunlit 143.
featureReviews.notes: The first build had the butt shadow without the tip highlight and read as wood grain; the pair is what makes it layers.

featureReviews.evidence: Eight knee braces and eight cord collars at the four post heads; two king posts, a ridge beam, six rafters and eight instanced purlins, all visible through the open gable ends at azimuth 90 and 270. Timber authored as the inverse of a two-point probe of the harness transfer and measured back at 134 / 111 / 111 / 94 across the four azimuths against a backdrop of 58.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's own timber value rendered at 49 -- below the backdrop -- on the first build; the lift and its arithmetic are on the material.

name: Nipa Thatch Canopy Module
nameTh: หลังคาจากใบจาก
notes: One bay of a modular outdoor roof kit: 4 x 4 m footprint on a 4 m grid, which divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2, so a canopy grid lands on the paving grid. Four corner posts, because the brief is a module that includes its own poles and must therefore stand alone; placed side by side the posts pair up at the shared edges, which is what a real market row looks like rather than a defect to design out. Gabled with the ridge across the module, so bays butted along the ridge axis continue one roof and bays butted across it read as a row of repeated gables. Eave at 2.4 m and ridge at 3.2 m, so a player walks under it with clearance. Open on all sides -- no walls, no infill, no hanging goods. Thatch depth is carried by the texture and the eave silhouette, not by modelled fronds, which would spend the whole triangle budget on the one thing a normal map does well.
